transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... I guess I'm here because I just can't seem to slow down. Since I stopped working, I'm just... up and moving all day. Going from one little job around the house to the next. It's like I still have a crew waiting on me or something.
How long has this feeling of needing to stay constantly busy and active been going on?
Well... I suppose it really became a problem after I retired. I used to do handyman work. Stopped doing that about... a year and two months ago. Just been like this since then.
Over this past year, have you noticed you need much less sleep than usual but still feel full of energy the next day?
No... I wouldn't say that. I still need my regular sleep. I just... I sleep fine.
Besides feeling like you need to stay busy, do you also find yourself worrying excessively about various things—like your health, finances, or family—more days than not?
No... not really. I don't think so. Just the usual, I guess. I'm not much of a worrier.
Aside from keeping yourself busy, do you often feel keyed up, on edge, or unable to relax?
No, I don't think so. Just... can't sit still, is all. I don't feel on edge.
Since you stopped working, have you been feeling down, sad, or less interested in things you used to enjoy?
No... not really. I feel fine. I still do my usual things... I'm not sad or anything. Just retired.
Has this constant need to stay busy caused any real problems for you—like trouble in your relationships, arguments with family, or difficulty relaxing enough to enjoy retirement?

Well... I don't know about real problems. But... my wife has had to take over keeping the calendar for us. Just... checking behind me on things. And I guess... I've had to apologize to the community center, and the garden group, more than once. Just for letting people down. But... yeah. That's about it.
